name: Minimum Projected Teaching Set Size
definition: For each concept, take the largest teaching-set size it has in any coordinate projection of $\mathcal{H}$. The **Minimum Projected Teaching Set Size** is the minimum of this quantity over all concepts in $\mathcal{H}$.
graph_summary: Minimum, over concepts, of their worst projected teaching-set size.

monotonic.proof: Counterexample on four coordinates: let H={0000,0010,0011,0101,0110,1010,1100,1101} and G=H\{1101}. Enumerating every coordinate projection and every teaching set gives the per-concept worst projected teaching sizes (3,4,3,3,3,3,3,2) for H and (3,4,3,3,3,3,3) for G. Hence TS_min^p(H)=2 whereas TS_min^p(G)=3, although G is a subfamily of H.

p_monotonic.proof: Choose a target h attaining the minimum for H. After projecting H to T, use the image of h as a target. Every further projection of that image is a projection of H on some U contained in T, and its teaching-set size is one of the candidates already bounded by the maximum used for h in H. Thus the minimum projected teaching-set size cannot increase.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, doubly monotonicity requires both subfamily monotonicity and projection monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

strictly_monotonic.proof: By definition, strictly monotonicity requires both doubly monotonicity and strict c-monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.
